title: Test-run query response outgrows the registration adapter's 64 KiB bound for a large uncommitted input, so registration is refused as invalid-response before any stage runs
outcome: A launcher's registration confirmation succeeds for an input of any supported size, because the confirmation reads a bounded projection rather than the full run detail, or the full detail no longer duplicates unbounded source identity.
acceptance: Registering a run whose uncommitted input has enough changed paths that its full source identity exceeds 64 KiB, then reading GET /api/test-runs/{id}?view=registration from the real host route, returns HTTP 200 with a body under 64 KiB that carries every identity field Engram's registration adapter (scripts/test-run-registration.mjs query()) checks, shown by a behavioural test; the end-to-end confirmation with Engram's shipped adapter is verified under Engram's w-b7d5132b2535.

The confirmation response stays within a documented bound independent of the input's changed-path count, and still carries every identity field the adapter checks (runId, owner and initiating session, registration state, durability, provenance, creatorPid, startedAt, detached, runDir, worktree, source).
The full run detail remains available to readers that ask for it; no source identity is truncated or dropped from the durable record.
